meta.name: OC Flood Hazard Areas Polygons
meta.description: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) produces Flood Insurance Rate maps and identifies Special Flood Hazard Areas as part of the National Flood Insurance Program's floodplain management. Special Flood Hazard Areas have regulations that include the mandatory purchase of flood insurance for holders of federally regulated mortgages. In addition, this layer can help planners and firms avoid areas of flood risk and also avoid additional cost to carry insurance for certain planned activities.This layer is derived from the May 7, 2025 version Flood Insurance Rate Map feature class S_FLD_HAZ_AR. The vector data were then flagged with an index of 94 classes, representing a unique combination of values displayed by three renderers. (In three resolutions the three renderers make nine processing templates.) Repair Geometry was run on the set of features, then the features were rasterized using the 94 class index at a resolutions of 10, 30, and 90 meters, using the Polygon to Raster tool and the "MAXIMUM_COMBINED_AREA" option. Projection: Web Mercator Auxiliary SphereData Coordinate System: USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic USGS version (contiguous US, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands), WGS 1984 Albers (Alaska), Hawaii Albers Equal Area Conic (Hawaii), Western Pacific Albers Equal Area Conic (Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, and American Samoa)Cell Sizes: 10 meters (default), 30 meters, and 90 metersData Date: May 7, 2025; Version: 2026.1, Updated: March 2026
meta.copyrightText: Dr. Kostas Alexandridis, GISP, Data Scientist, OC Public Works, OC Survey Geospatial Services for the Orange County data and project extent processing. Original data from FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps, and ESRI Living Atlas.

meta.name: Outfall Locations
meta.description: This feature class includes data collected by OC Environmental Resources pursuant to the monitoring and reporting requirements of the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Fifth Term Permit (Order R9-2013-001, as amended by Orders No. 2015-001 and R9-2015-0100, NPDES CAS0109266) issued by the San Diego Regional Board (RWQCB). The data contains the locations of municipal separate storm sewer system (MS4) outfalls features. The dataset was expanded in August 2017 to include North and Central Orange County outfalls.Initial outfalls were added using aerial imagery, OCFCD drainage facility maps, and information from other NPDES monitoring programs.Important Fields:INSPECTED - Identifies whether the outfall has verified by field visit, could not be found, or removed from the inventory.GlobalID - Relates the outfall with field observations.
